tasks.title: pending_outbound approval state machine + DB guard
tasks.notes: Guard foundation done (commit f8740ce). REMAINING: approve/decline/expire transitions, authenticated one-time token consumption, claim->deliver->mark-sent worker.

prep.what: Finish the 3-state approval flow on `PendingOutbound` — approve/decline/expire transitions, one-time token consumption, and the claim→deliver→mark-sent worker.
prep.understand: The guard foundation is done (commit f8740ce): `PendingOutbound` with `approvalTokenHash`/`expiresAt`/`consumedAt` is in place, DB constraints enforce state integrity. Now you're building Phase 2 — actual state transitions and the worker that delivers approved messages.
approach: Add `approve(token)`, `decline()`, `expire()` methods to `PendingOutbound` — enforce one-time token via `approvalTokenHash` check and set `consumedAt` timestamp on use.
Build the auth endpoint for approval/decline links — single-use token flow, no session required, returns a clear success/already-used/expired response.
Wire the `claim→deliver→mark_sent` worker: poll approved records, call the outbound channel, mark status `sent`.
Extend `test:outbound` (currently 7 checks) to cover the new transitions and token-replay rejection.
resources: Commit f8740ce (guard foundation — start here to see what's already wired)

tasks.title: Per-tenant DEK envelope encryption (master key off-box)
tasks.notes: Mechanism done (commits f1e9bea + 1057e64). REMAINING: wire the real KekProvider KMS driver (GCP KMS recommended in SERVICES doc).

prep.what: Fill the `KekProvider` seam with a real KMS driver so per-tenant DEKs are wrapped by an off-box master key — not just the dev env key-ring.
prep.understand: The full AES-256-GCM mechanism is done: `KekProvider` seam exists with env key-ring (dev) + KMS stub, `tenantId` as AAD, race-safe DEK resolver, ALS-scoped API, 14 tests green. The remaining piece is one real KMS implementation. SERVICES.md recommends GCP Cloud KMS.
approach: Open SERVICES-AND-INTEGRATIONS.md, find the KMS section — confirm GCP Cloud KMS is the right call (or make the AWS KMS call if you prefer).
Implement `GcpKmsKekProvider` (or your chosen driver): `wrapDek(tenantId, plaintextDek)` and `unwrapDek(tenantId, ciphertext)` using the Cloud KMS Node.js SDK (`@google-cloud/kms`).
Wire the provider in the production/staging config, test fail-closed behavior when credentials are absent.
Run `test:crypto` (14 checks) to confirm no regressions, then smoke-test a wrap+unwrap round-trip with a real (or sandbox) KMS key.
resources: Commits f1e9bea + 1057e64 (full mechanism — read before touching anything)
GCP Cloud KMS Node.js SDK: `@google-cloud/kms` npm docs
Existing `test:crypto` suite (14 checks must stay green)

tasks.title: Append-only audit log for privileged agent actions
tasks.notes: EXISTS: ActivityLog model + lib/activity-log.ts (tenant-scoped, generic). NET-NEW: record AGENT actions — tenant, tool, recipient, model, input provenance, human-confirmed — immutable, token-scrubbed.

prep.what: Extend `ActivityLog` to record privileged AGENT actions separately from human activity — immutable rows with PII/token scrubbing, wired into the approve/send flow.
prep.understand: `ActivityLog` model and `lib/activity-log.ts` already exist for human activity. You need an agent-specific log type with stronger guarantees: no UPDATE/DELETE allowed, `properties` must be scrubbed of tokens/PII before insert. This is PRD §7/§10's breach detector + liability shield.
approach: Add an `agent_action` type discriminator to `ActivityLog` (or a separate table if you want a cleaner schema split) — fields: `tenant_id`, `tool`, `recipient_id`, `model`, `input_provenance`, `human_confirmed`, `properties` (scrubbed JSON).
Create `logAgentAction()` in `lib/activity-log.ts` — enforces append-only (no update/delete path), strips token-shaped strings and PII from `properties` before persist.
Wire the call into the `PendingOutbound` approve flow (t8) and the DEK usage path (t9) so every privileged agent dispatch is logged.
Write a test verifying that real token values (`sk_...`, `Bearer ...`) don't appear in stored `properties` after a `logAgentAction()` call.
resources: `PendingOutbound` approve flow (t8, being built this morning)

tasks.title: NotificationChannel abstraction + ChatwootChannel (SMS, live-tested)
tasks.notes: Chatwoot SMS channel live-tested. Abstraction layer deferred (spec §5.2): OutboundMessage/NotificationRecipient VOs, label()/medium()/supports(), sent=blue badge NOT built. Unblocks t69/t70/t71.

prep.what: Build the `NotificationChannel` abstraction layer — `ChatwootChannel` is live and tested; now formalize the interface so future channels plug in cleanly.
prep.understand: Chatwoot SMS is working in production. What's missing is the formal contract: `OutboundMessage` and `NotificationRecipient` value objects (spec §5.2 R15), `label()`, `medium()`, `supports()` interface methods, and the `sent`=blue-badge UI contract. This is a required unlock for t69, t70, t71 (next notification channels).
approach: Define the `NotificationChannel` interface with `label(): string`, `medium(): string`, `supports(recipient: NotificationRecipient): bool`, `send(msg: OutboundMessage, recipient: NotificationRecipient): Promise<void>`.
Create `OutboundMessage` VO and `NotificationRecipient` VO per spec §5.2 R15 — keep them value objects (immutable, no DB model).
Refactor `ChatwootChannel` to implement the new interface — should be a drop-in refactor since the underlying logic doesn't change.
Update the `sent`=blue-badge UI to pull from `channel.medium()` so it stays correct for future channels.
resources: t69, t70, t71 task titles (downstream channels — skim to understand what the interface must support)

tasks.title: Secrets in .env.production (Stripe both modes, Chatwoot, mail)

prep.what: Populate `.env.production` with all real secret values needed for go-live: Stripe test + live keys, Chatwoot API token, and mail credentials.
prep.understand: Without these, Stripe webhooks fail silently, Chatwoot notifications don't fire, and password-reset emails are dead on arrival. This is a hard gate for t36 (DO droplet deploy). The values live in `.env.production` (gitignored) — don't commit them.
approach: Open Stripe dashboard → API keys: grab `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` (live `sk_live_...`), `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, and the webhook signing secret `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Also grab the test-mode equivalents if you want a smoke test before flipping live.
Open Chatwoot admin panel → Settings → API tokens: copy the API token for `CHATWOOT_API_TOKEN` + `CHATWOOT_API_URL`.
Pull mail credentials (SMTP host/user/pass, or Postmark/Mailgun API key) from your mail provider dashboard.
Write all values to `.env.production`, then run `php artisan config:cache` and `php artisan config:show` to verify no missing required keys.
resources: Stripe dashboard → API keys + Webhooks sections
Chatwoot admin panel → Settings → API tokens
Mail provider dashboard (Postmark, Mailgun, or SMTP creds)
`.env.example` in the repo — key names to fill
t36 task (DO droplet deploy — this is its secrets gate)
